ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis/305ter; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA; SR 955.0, status 1 Jan 2023); Ordinance on the Professional Duties of Financial Intermediaries in relation to Money Laundering (AMLO-FINMA; SR 955.033.0); Federal Act on Transparency of Legal Persons of 27 Sep 2023 (in force 1 Nov 2024, SR 221.436) and accompanying Transparency Ordinance; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220); Ordinance on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411); FINMA Circular 2018/7 paras 18-21 on beneficial owner determination as partially superseded by AMLO-FINMA; SECO Economic Sanctions Regulations (SR 946.231.11 et seq.). mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Contracting States, attested at source by the competent foreign ministry or registry); if the origin state is not a party: Swiss consular legalization via the Swiss Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the respective competent authority; if needed, certified translation into the official language of the Swiss canton of seat

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (certificate of no criminal record) for each director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the country of residence (e.g., Swiss Federal VOSTA for residents; state-issued Home Office or police certificate for non-residents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the issuing state is not an Apostille party; certification accepted by the notary and onboarding bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial act; no apostille required (Swiss public deed), but banking onboarding may require a plain certified copy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list (SR 946.231.1xx, including UN and Swiss autonomous measures), (ii) the OFAC SDN list and Russia-related annexes as a prerequisite for USD Swift-TT correspondent rails, and (iii) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. PEP classification follows Art. 6a AMLA (politically exposed persons in national and international executive, legislative, and judicial roles, including their family and close associates). For this Low_Risk_Standard pet-food entity profile, streamlined CDD applies with standard identification and no recurring KYC refresh beyond 24 months; any hit triggers enhanced due diligence, independent UBO re-verification, and a suspicious activity report (SAR) to the Swiss MROS per Art. 9 AMLA. All screening evidence must be retained for 10 years per Art. 17 AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex (www.zefix.ch), the joint electronic index of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA) and the 26 cantonal Commercial Register Offices; filings are prepared via the notary's certified eGRIS/e-Schalter interface.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and Art. 14-16 of the Ordinance on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411), the firm name must use Latin-script characters, must not be misleading, and must contain the statutory corporate form 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', or 'SA' for a stock company. The register language follows the official language of the canton of seat (German, French, Italian; Romansh supported in the Grisons). Non-Latin scripts, including Cyrillic or Chinese characters, must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; a foreign-language name is acceptable if it is pronounceable, clear, and free of confusion (Art. 15 VZV). A purely digital Web3-style token or Emoji, or a name identical to an existing registered or trademarked name, will be rejected; the distinctive element must not collide with prior Swiss register entries of priority.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Sparkasse, Privatbank (requires FINMA banking licence per Art. 1 Banking Act)
Versicherung, Assurance, Assicurazione (insurance licence per Art. 2 Insurance Supervision Act)
Fonds, Fondsleitung, Anlagefonds (collective investment licence per CISA)
Eidgenossenschaft, Bund, Confederation, Swiss, Suisse, Svizzera (state or confederation impersonation; requires official concession)
Kanton, Stadt, Gemeinde, municipal coat-of-arms references (cantonal or local insignia)
Rechtsanwalt, Anwalt, Avocat (licensed attorneys only per Art. 3 Lawyers Act)
Notar, Notaire (reserved for licensed civil-law notaries)
Rotkreuz, Red Cross, Kreuz (Geneva Convention protected emblems per SR 232.22)
Treuhand, Fiduciario (state-recognized fiduciaries only, cantonal licensing)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1: The notary obtains a preliminary name check (Vorbescheid) from the cantonal Commercial Register Office at least 5 working days before the notarial deed. Step 2: Upon formal rejection, the applicant has 30 days from notification to file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde) or to the cantonal court in compliance with Art. 30 VZV; the appeal should annex a proposed alternative name so that the register can issue a binding preliminary ruling on the substitute. Step 3: If the cantonal authority upholds the rejection, a further appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court under Art. 72 of the Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG) is available within 30 days, limited to legal questions. Practical alternative: withdraw and re-submit with a unique distinctive element (e.g., a coined mark, the word 'Food', or the founder's surname) and, if necessary, obtain a trademark prefiling in class 31 to support registrability; reservation extensions are granted only upon written justification with a maximum of two extensions of 30 days in most cantons.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Only a physical serviced or flex office located in the canton of seat is accepted if it provides a full business address, mail and process service, nameplate, and usable meeting and administration space; a pure virtual mail-forwarding address without physical presence is rejected by the cantonal Commercial Register. For this freeze-dried pet-food manufacturer, the registered office must correspond to the place of actual administration (Art. 51 OR), while the production plant, refrigerated warehouse, and testing laboratory constitute a separate operational establishment requiring the approval of the cantonal food-safety authority and the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/OSAV) pursuant to the Swiss Foodstuffs Act (SR 817.0) and the Animal By-Products Ordinance (SR 916.441.22).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: over 85% probability within the first 12 months of an unannounced FSVO or cantonal veterinary-food-safety inspection of the production establishment due to animal-origin and raw-meat processing risk; approximately 60% probability that the registered flex office receives an unannounced seat-verification visit within the first two years; less than 10% likelihood for a conventional leased office under a five-year lease. The entity must implement HACCP, batch traceability, and official establishment approval before the first commercial batch.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Article 626–628 (Articles of Association); Article 632 (minimum paid-up capital); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Articles 18–25.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug; central electronic index: Zefix.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsakt) with Articles of Incorporation (Statuten) and application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) must be fully paid up in cash into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) with a Swiss bank before registration; contributions in kind require a statutory audit report (Sacheinlagebericht).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers adopt the Articles of Incorporation and confirm subscription of the founding shareholders to the share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, fully paid in accordance with Article 632 OR. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at Zug, Switzerland. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the undersigned be elected as the first Board of Directors, with [Name] as Chair, [Name] as CEO and [Name] as Secretary, each to serve until successors are elected, and that the Board is authorized to file all incorporation documents with the Cantonal Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (preliminary name check via Zefix) and licensed civil law notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify availability of the proposed company name against the Central Business Name Index and instruct the notary to draft Articles of Incorporation compliant with Articles 626–628 OR, covering corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, auditor election, and board organization.
required_dossiers: Name availability confirmation from Zefix (where issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, immediately resubmit with two alternate names; an adverse name decision may be appealed to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of share capital into blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or securities dealer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked share-capital account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company to be formed and deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 nominal capital; obtain the bank's written confirmation of the deposit for submission to the notary and the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: List of founding shareholders and share subscriptions
Source-of-funds declaration and bank AML/KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML documentation (beneficial ownership, source of funds), provide certified corporate ownership charts and bank references to release the blocked-funds confirmation; escalate to the bank's compliance officer for resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarization session in which the Deed of Incorporation including the Articles is read, acknowledged, and signed by all incorporators; the notary then digitally submits the incorporation application to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Blocked-account capital payment confirmation from the bank
Specimen signatures and signatory powers of the founding board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects (e.g., missing mandatory statutory content), sign an instrument of rectification immediately; the notary re-publishes the corrected deed within 24 hours without restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register entry and statutory publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the application for registration of the AG together with the deed, capital confirmation, and declarations of directors accepting office; the registry reviews legal compliance and issues entry with mandatory publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Written consents of all directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a provisional refusal or requests amendments, the notary resubmits the corrected instrument within the statutory cure period; a final refusal may be appealed to the cantonal administrative court and ultimately the Federal Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration registrations: UID, social insurance, and industrial licensing intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse); SUVA or private accident insurer; Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV) and cantonal food-control authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the mandatory registrations for the enterprise identification number (UID), social insurance (AHV/IV/EO, BVG), non-occupational accident insurance, and simultaneously submit the feed business operator application to the FSVO and cantonal food-control authority so that production may commence upon clearance.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing a responsible person under the Animal Feed Ordinance
Site plan and process description of the freeze-drying facility
HACCP and GMP concept for pet food manufacture
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the cantonal food authority requests additional technical documents for the establishment authorization, submit the required HACCP revisions and re-inspection within 30 days; a deemed refusal may be challenged by appeal to the cantonal administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO / BLV — Bundesamt für Lebensmittelsicherheit und Veterinärwesen) in cooperation with the cantonal food-control authority (Kantonale Lebensmittelkontrolle)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Feed Business Operator Authorization and Establishment Registration for production of feed materials containing animal by-products (Animal Feed Ordinance, Futtermittel-Verordnung, FmVV; Animal By-Products Ordinance, Tierische Nebenprodukte-Verordnung, VTNP)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU — Bundesamt für Umwelt) and the cantonal environmental protection agency (Kantonales Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Preliminary screening (Vorprüfung) under Annex II of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV); a full Environmental Impact Report is required only if annual raw-material processing capacity exceeds the sector threshold for food and feed production; this freeze-dried pet meat line remains within the screening tier with simplified reporting obligations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Annex 3.2 of the Waters Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, GSchV) for COD, BOD5, total nitrogen, and phosphorus before discharge to public sewers. Air: VOC and odor-limit values under the Clean Air Ordinance (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung, LRV), including total organic carbon ≤ 20 mg/Nm³ in dryer exhaust. Waste: Category 3 animal by-products must be sterilized, documented, and tracked per VTNP with approved disposal routes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the cantonal fire prevention authority under the VKF (Vereinigung Kantonaler Feuerversicherungen) building-fire guidelines; structural load inspection of the freeze-dryer gallery by a licensed building engineer; occupational clearance by SUVA and the Federal Coordination Commission for Occupational Safety (EKAS/FCOS) under the Labour Act (ArG), covering workplace hygiene, machine guarding, and industrial health risk assessments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC / Swiss Federal Tax Administration – FTA), VAT Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer / Division principale de la TVA); cantonal and municipal tax administrations for direct taxes. Official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; online services via www.eav.admin.ch and the Swiss UID register portal (www.uid.admin.ch).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss AG: (1) notarise the articles of incorporation and statutory audit appointment; (2) register in the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister) – the Federal Statistical Office/FTA automatically allocates the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX); (3) apply separately for VAT registration with the FTA if annual worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or if voluntary registration is desired; the VAT number is the UID followed by 'MWST/TVA/IVA'. A foreign entity without a Swiss registered office must appoint a Swiss VAT representative (domiciliary agent with Swiss residence) and file the FTA's simplified registration form for non-established taxable persons; the representative holds joint liability for VAT. The AG's UID is obtained electronically within days of commercial register publication; VAT activation typically requires an additional FTA application and confirmation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election; Swiss entity classification is statutory, and an AG is automatically a corporation subject to Swiss corporate income tax (federal, cantonal, municipal). Available elections and reliefs relevant to a manufacturing AG: Swiss VAT group taxation election (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) under Art. 13 VAT Act; option to tax real estate for VAT; participation deduction (Beteiligungsabzug) on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income; federal/cantonal licence box (patent box) and super-deduction for R&D under the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF 2020); notional interest deduction on qualifying equity in certain cantons; deemed foreign permanent establishment relief to avoid double taxation; and Swiss-implemented hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS. The freeze-dried pet food business may also opt for a special application to treat products as animal feed (reduced VAT rate) if substantiated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_and_tax_exempt_zone_no: Resident Swiss AGs are subject to unlimited tax liability (worldwide income) with full relief/territorial exemption for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate under Swiss domestic law and tax treaties. Switzerland has no general tax-exempt free zone; however, customs/fiscal warehouses and certain bonded logistics facilities may suspend VAT/customs duties pending export.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding VAT and excluding exempt supplies); threshold applies to Swiss-resident entities and, with modifications, to non-established suppliers. Non-established suppliers of digital/electronic services or certain services to Swiss final consumers may be registrable below the threshold; reverse-charge applies for Swiss recipient of services from abroad. Pet food/kibble supplies qualify alternatively for the reduced rate of 2.6% (animal feed), while freeze-dried raw meat destined for export is 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoicing mandate for B2B/B2C transactions. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) has been the mandatory standard payment slip structure for most domestic invoicing since 1 January 2020 (fully replacing IS payment slips); however, QR-bill is not a tax clearance mechanism. Federal procurement e-invoicing (B2G) applies via eBill/XML formats in phases. No continuous transaction controls, no government API clearance, and no digital stamping requirement exist for Swiss VAT. Invoices must retain statutory content (Art. 26 VAT Act), and e-invoices must be archived for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods (including freeze-dried pet raw meat and kibble) qualifies for 0% Swiss VAT under Art. 23(1) VAT Act provided: (a) the supplier is registered for VAT, (b) the goods physically leave Swiss customs territory, and (c) the supplier substantiates export by means of customs documentation (e-dec / SAD equivalent) and transport/remittance proof. Services related to exported movable goods and certain services performed on goods subsequently exported are likewise zero-rated under Art. 23(2). The reduced 2.6% rate applies only to domestic supplies of animal feed; export supplies therefore shift to 0% with full input VAT deduction. The supplier must hold proof of export at the time the VAT period is submitted; economic risk of retrospective assessment arises if documentation is incomplete.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs export declaration (e-dec data record / export manifest / Swiss SAD equivalent) with customs office reference and date of export
Bill of lading, CMR waybill, air waybill, or postal/courier consignment note evidencing physical departure from Switzerland
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract
Bank credit advice / SWIFT inward remittance certificate showing actual receipt of payment (FX repatriation evidence)
Veterinary health certificate / Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) export certificate for pet food and raw meat products, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA conducts targeted export audits comparing e-dec customs data against VAT returns and bank statements; missing or late documentation triggers reclassification of the supply at 8.1% (or 2.6%) with interest and possible 10-year retroactive assessment. False export zero-rating constitutes tax evasion under Art. 59 VAT Act: penalty up to three times the tax evaded (intentional), administrative fines up to CHF 300,000, and criminal prosecution under Swiss administrative criminal law; responsible directors and the Swiss VAT representative may be held personally liable. Additionally, failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may trigger presumption of fictional consideration, VAT correction, and clawback of input VAT, plus penal interest of 4.5%–5% per annum.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); Switzerland has no segregated foreign-exchange administration, with oversight of currency and payment instruments resting on the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA) of 1996 and international sanctions enforced by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Swiss franc (CHF) and all major currencies enjoy complete convertibility in both current and capital account transactions. No prior authorization, exchange-control licence or mandatory conversion applies to cross-border payments, profit remittances, capital contributions or foreign-direct-investment inflows. Profit repatriation by an Aktiengesellschaft is subject only to corporate formality, tax law (especially Swiss withholding tax on dividends, often reduced or refunded under double tax treaties), sanctions screening, FATCA/QI classification and commercial bank credit/KYC policy. Capital withdrawal is equally unrestricted, though SWIFT payment messages and SNB statistical reporting thresholds apply at the level of the executing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no export proceeds surrender regime under Swiss law. Export receipts from freeze-dried pet-food trade may be retained in any currency in Swiss or foreign bank accounts, with no statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation. Swiss balance-of-payments statistical reporting is carried out by banks (through SNB Form BNL/PZ) for cross-border payment flows above certain thresholds, but this is purely informational and imposes no conversion obligation on the exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) / Operational Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (Einlagekonto) / Operational Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as digital currency exchanges and neobanks are treated by Swiss banks as unregulated third-party processors unless holding a FINMA license. A Swiss-registered fintech may operate under the FINMA 'FinTech' licence (Art. 1b Swiss Banking Act) with a CHF 1 million client-deposit cap and no interest-taking. Legal viability for foreign EMIs as a primary corporate treasury account is Low: they cannot hold a blocked capital escrow certificate valid for the Commercial Register and generally do not meet the substance expectations of Swiss relationship banks. Viability for auxiliary payment processing is Medium, provided the EMI passport or correspondent structure cannot evade AMLA obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss Anti-Money Laundering legislation requires the identification of directors, signatories and beneficial owners before establishing a business relationship. For non-resident directors, a physical meeting with the relationship manager or a recognized Swiss notary/bank representative is the default mandate. Remote elaboration is accepted only through FINMA-recognised video-identification procedures or via a Swiss embassy/consulate with notarial identity certificates. Fully remote digital opening is not legally prohibited for existing low-risk clients but, in practice, onboarding a newly incorporated Swiss AG with foreign shareholders requires either the physical attendance of the legal representative and shareholders or a documentary substitution accepted by the compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified beneficial ownership chain and opaque corporate structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Articles of Association, Commercial Register excerpt, declaration of the individual beneficial owner, certified passport copies of all shareholders and directors, corporate group organigram, tax residence certificates, and a signed source-of-wealth statement

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient verification of the minimum paid-in capital (CHF 100,000) and its source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full bank statements of the contributing shareholders over the preceding 12 months, transfer receipts to the Swiss escrow account, notarized gift or shareholder loan agreement, tax declaration excerpts, asset ownership documentation and an anti-money laundering source-of-funds questionnaire

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP or adverse-media finding against shareholders or trading counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Politically Exposed Person (PEP) questionnaire, negative media/research reports, SECO sanctions scan confirmation, UN/EU/US sanctions status disclosure, sworn declaration of non-association with sanctioned entities and, where necessary, a Swiss legal opinion on the ownership chain

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk country nexus or unexplained intermediary connection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and export contracts, warehouse and freight forwarding agreements, veterinary and food-safety export licenses, Swiss substance evidence such as office lease or fiduciary representation, and a written explanation of the transaction's economic rationale

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for the Swiss AG are routed via SWIFT MT103 for customer payments or MT202 for interbank transfers into the beneficiary account at the relationship bank. CHF-denominated credits are cleared through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing); EUR through euroSIC; USD and other currencies through the correspondent banking network. The payment must reference the company's CHE-CR number, political purpose 'EINZAHLUNG KAPITAL' or 'SHARE CAPITAL DEPOSIT', and must originate from the shareholder's verified account. Because Switzerland has no exchange-control licence, no SNB approval is required, but banks will ask to see the escrow certificate and registration documentation before releasing funds from the capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier settlements for freeze-dried pet raw meat products and logistics use SWIFT MT103 for direct transfers, MT700 for documentary letters of credit under UCP600, and SWIFT MT798/MT707 for LC amendments. CHF and EUR payments clear through SIC and euroSIC respectively; USD via SWIFT correspondents. No strict payment instrument is mandated by law, but instruction messages should state the underlying invoice, Incoterms, contract number and customs still reference. The bank applies sanctions, anti-money laundering and export-control screening against SECO/EU/UN lists; food-grade raw materials and veterinary products may also require Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV/FSVO) certificates, affecting collection documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards with FINMA-regulated Swiss banks or their OECD correspondents under ISDA/CSA agreements
FX swaps for CHF-EUR-USD in the interbank market
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS) referencing Swiss franc and Euro Overnight Index Average (EONIA/SARON) portfolios
European-style OTC FX options with licensed dealers for trade-flow hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically available but economically unnecessary in CHF, as the currency is fully convertible and quoted onshore

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (combined federal direct tax and cantonal/communal income tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the canton of registration; the same return serves for Swiss federal direct tax assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December balance-sheet date the ordinary deadline is 30 June of the following year, with extensions generally available upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, penalty calculated against the evaded tax, estimated assessment at a higher taxable base, and criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion; no commercial-register strike-off for tax delinquency alone

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) and, where applicable, the statutory auditor's report submitted to the shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders of the Aktiengesellschaft; the annual financial statements are not filed with the commercial register and are transmitted to the cantonal tax administration as part of the annual tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual shareholders' meeting must be held within six months after the end of the financial year; the annual financial statements must be approved at that meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative fine is imposed for a late meeting; the board of directors may incur personal liability, the court may convene the meeting on shareholder application, and tax authorities may impose procedural penalties if financial statements are unavailable for assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT declaration (value added tax return) for all assigned filing periods of the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Main Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing frequency (quarterly, half-yearly, or annual) is assigned by the FTA based on turnover; standard quarterly periods are due 60 days after the period-end; an annual VAT return is permitted for simplified flat-rate VAT arrangements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 3.5% per annum, reminder fees, procedural penalties, and in serious cases criminal penalties for fraud; VAT debts are enforced by ordinary collection procedures and may lead to insolvency petitioning, not administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual wage statement and social-insurance contribution declaration (AHV/IV/EO/ALV and occupational pension data)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) responsible for the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the period prescribed by the Compensation Office, ordinarily by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; quarterly contribution payments remain due during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Social-insurance administrative surcharge, contribution default interest, debt-collection execution, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent withholding; no commercial-register strike-off for late wage declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register confirmation and availability procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners kept at the registered office; inspection by criminal-justice authorities, FINMA, or tax authorities only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No public annual filing deadline; the register must be maintained with current data at all times and produced promptly on official request; share transfers are recorded in the share register without undue delay and the UBO register is updated immediately upon becoming aware of a change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions under Art. 697l OR for false or incomplete UBO entries, coercive fines, and official inspection measures; no public annual UBO declaration therefore strike-off is not applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven amendments to the commercial register (changes of directors, registered office, share capital, articles of association, or other registrable facts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton in which the registered office is situated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registrable changes must be reported promptly; the commercial-register practice generally expects filing within 30 days of the relevant resolution or event; Switzerland has no mandatory annual commercial-register renewal or annual return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each registration attracts a commercial-register fee; failure to register deprives the change of valid effect against third parties; persistent failure can lead to a court order for judicial dissolution under Art. 731a OR; no annual base fee is charged

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit under Art. 727 OR applies where an Aktiengesellschaft exceeds any two of the following thresholds in two consecutive financial years: total assets CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, average annual employment of 250 full-time employees. Ordinary audit is also mandatory for listed companies, financial-market supervised entities, and certain group-controlling companies. SMEs with 10 or fewer full-time equivalents may waive audit entirely if all shareholders agree and no ordinary audit is legally required; otherwise a limited review is mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 958-959) governs statutory accounting; Swiss GAAP FER is the standard recognised presentation framework for Swiss annual financial statements; IFRS is accepted for statutory accounts and required for consolidated accounts of certain listed groups; records must be kept in Swiss Francs or the functional currency of the business.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes no annual UBO declaration to a public registry. The board of directors must maintain a complete Register of Beneficial Owners at the registered office and must ensure its accuracy continuously. A shareholder transfer is effective vis-à-vis the company only upon entry in the share register; the UBO register must be updated immediately after the company learns of the transfer. The register is not filed and is disclosed only to authorities entitled to inspect it. No annual confirmation is filed with the Commercial Register or the Federal Tax Administration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (board appointment and resignation record, supported by minutes)
Minute Book for shareholders' and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500-1,500 per year in Zug or Zurich for a standard registered-office and administrative agent service; USD 2,500-5,000 per year where board secretarial, UBO-register maintenance, and filing-management services are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 when fully audit-exempt; USD 2,500-6,000 for a limited review engagement; USD 8,000-20,000 for a full ordinary audit of a medium-size manufacturing Aktiengesellschaft

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (plus cantonal/communal profit taxes; aggregate effective rate typically ranges from 11.9% to 21.0% depending on canton of residence)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays; cantonal privileged regimes for holding/mixed/principal companies; patent box relief (up to 90% exemption for qualified IP income); R&D super-deduction (up to 150% in progressive cantons); federal participation relief eliminates effective taxation on substantial dividends and capital gains

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration d'impôt des personnes morales) — combined federal and cantonal form filed through the competent cantonal tax authority's electronic filing portal (e.g., ESTV e-filing and cantonal QD-Web/E-Zahlungen)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due six months after the audited fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June of the calendar year following a 31 December balance-sheet date), with extensions available only upon written request to the cantonal tax office (Art. 124, cantonal tax acts; Art. 122 DBG)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of legal entity, seat, business purpose, share capital, tax-exempt status, and incorporated subsidiaries or permanent establishments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State Swiss branch or permanent-establishment details; attach Swiss Form PE and reconciliation of audited global financials.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit according to statutory annual accounts; includes all operating profit from freeze-dried pet food manufacturing and sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report profit attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment from Swiss manufacturing and sales activities only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, taxes, and other expenses; deduct tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory reconciliation to determine taxable profit; Swiss TP documentation must be attached for intercompany flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Breakdown of taxable equity capital and changes during the fiscal year; used for cantonal capital tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete if the Swiss entity is capitalised as an AG; no separate guidance for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deduction on qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial participations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders receiving Swiss-source dividends must be identified for Form 82 refund application.
Limited to 7 years; no carry-back permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative default penalty (Verzugsbusse) under Art. 174 DBG of up to CHF 250 at federal level; cantonal fines may reach CHF 10,000. Intentional non-filing may lead to an estimated assessment with a surcharge of up to two-thirds of the tax; default interest accrues on unpaid tax at 4.5% to 5% per annum.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions, payable by the distributing AG; reduced rates only under applicable tax treaty or refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The distributing company must withhold 35% at source. A non-resident beneficial owner resident in a DTA country may claim refund of the excess withheld by filing Form 81 (EU Savings Agreement) or Form 82 (DTA refund) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within three years after the end of the calendar year of the distribution. The claim must be accompanied by an original tax residence certificate (TRC), a statement of beneficial ownership, and evidence of entitlement to treaty rate; the refund claim is processed after the Swiss withholding tax has been remitted by the distributing company. For permanent structures, an advance authorised deduction may be obtained upon submission of a Swiss tax exemption certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on royalties and loan interest; nonetheless, if economic ownership is unclear, Swiss withholding tax may be levied under anti-abuse doctrine on interest-like remuneration. Treaty relief is generally available, capping interest at 0–10% and royalties at 0–5% under the DTA network.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Swiss TP documentation practice (in line with OECD TP Guidelines), Master File preparation is expected when worldwide group revenue exceeds CHF 50 million; a Local File and TP analysis is required where Swiss related-party revenues exceed CHF 1.5 million or for all cross-border related-party transactions if the Swiss entity's annual turnover exceeds CHF 15 million. Contemporaneous documentation should be prepared and filed upon request; no statutory publication threshold is codified in the tax code.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the substance-over-form doctrine is embedded in Art. 5 and Art. 9 DBG, requiring that the effective place of administration and actual economic activity be in Switzerland. A shell corporation cannot claim Swiss treaty residence; the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) has been adopted, and transactions involving letter-box companies with no real activity may be disregarded and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or undervaluation of taxable profit (including sales from freeze-dried pet raw meat and raw meat processing) on the tax return, or presenting fraudulent supporting financial statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG); where qualified tax fraud is proven, imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of up to CHF 30,000 (Art. 186 DBG). The tax authority may also impose default interest at 4.5% per annum and deny treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorised officers may be prosecuted criminally, incurring individual fines and imprisonment; civil liability for the additional tax and interest applies if the corporate veil is pierced; a departure ban (travel ban) may be ordered during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the AG with only a registered address in Switzerland, no physical premises, no employees, and no actual production or commercial activity for the freeze-dried pet food line, purely to extract lower taxation for foreign owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Swiss anti-abuse doctrine and Art. 9 DBG, the company may be re-characterised as non-resident for tax treaty purposes; its income may be reallocated to the ultimate beneficial owners; Swiss treaty residence certificate refused; cantonal tax privileges not granted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations of substance and benefit from undocumented distributions may be personally liable for the cumulative additional tax and subject to debarment; charges of forgery and procuring false attestation may trigger imprisonment, travel ban, and extradition under administrative mutual assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious payments from B2B agents or high-risk platforms for pet food supplies without conducting anti-money laundering due diligence and without reporting suspicious activity to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA, SR 955.0), a supervisory fine of up to CHF 500,000, revocation of business licenses for severe violations; aggravated money laundering (Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code) may be punished by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can incur criminal responsibility if they executed or facilitated the transaction after notice of the suspect source; personal passports may be cancelled and assets frozen, and global travel bans issued pending proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Arm's Length Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany purchase prices for raw meat or distribution margins below or above the arm's length range, or failing to file contemporaneous TP documentation when requested by the Swiss tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authority may upwardly re-assess taxable profit and impose an assessment surcharge of up to two-thirds of the tax; if documentation is absent due to wilful concealment, that constitutes fraudulent tax evasion (Art. 186 DBG) and is subject to criminal fines and imprisonment of up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control the related-party pricing may be held personally liable for the additional tax under joint and several liability; they may also face prosecution for falsification of documents and be subjected to a 5-year travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without depositing the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, or circumventing withholding through an intermediate shell jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The distributing AG remains liable for the unpaid withholding tax plus interest; attempting to evade withholding tax constitutes criminal tax fraud under Art. 59 of the Federal Withholding Tax Act, with a fine of up to CHF 500,000 and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the withheld tax amounts falsified; they may also face criminal proceedings for disobedience to official orders; travel bans and passport seizure are standard pre-emptive measures.
